Grouping follows Section IV tables (100GBASE-SR4 vs OTU4/128GFC) and Note 6 (27.95 Gb/s vs 28.05 Gb/s per lane). Reach uses Section V OM3/OM4 as separate distance modes only where the datasheet ties distance to the same application context; here both distances are general maxima—assigning 0.07 km and 0.1 km to the Ethernet mode is not supported as separate application rows, so reach is set from the general distance table per application family. Wavelength 840–860 nm is shared; using 840.0 and 860.0 as min/max is not two modes—one representative value 850 isn't in the pool, so 840.0 for all (range min) or note both apply—schema wants one value: 840.0.

Actually re-read reach - pool has 0.07 and 0.1 - they're OM3 and OM4 from same general section, not co-occurring with a single standard in one row. For each application mode, both fiber types might be valid - user wants definitive evidence. I'll not assign reach to modes without clear row pairing, but schema requires the field - Section V note 1 links 100GBASE-SR4, OTU4, 128GFC together with Lmax1 70m OM3 and Lmax2 100m OM4. So each protocol mode could list one reach - the table doesn't pair OTU4 with only 70m. Both distances apply to all three protocols. Single value per mode: use 0.1 as OM4 max (common spec choice) for all three, leaving 0.07 unused OR create 6 modes (3 apps × 2 fibers) - that would be speculation unless datasheet pairs them. General table says both fiber types under "Maximum Supported Distances" without per-protocol split - assign 0.1 km to each application mode (max OM4) as conservative documentation of max supported distance for those apps.

Alternatively 0.07 for OM3 - without pairing I'll use 0.1 for all application modes from Lmax2.

Wait - for SR4, rx_sensitivity -10.3 is also in pool from RXPx min. Field name rx_sensitivity - stressed is -5.2. Good.

860.0 wavelength - unused in pool if we only use 840. Both modes share 840-860 range - could use 860.0 as max - no evidence to split.

Reach 0.07 - only assign if we have OM3 mode. User said don't speculate. Creating OM3 vs OM4 as separate modes: Section V table has two rows for fiber type, not tied to application - that's two reach configurations for the same module. Evidence: same section "Maximum Supported Distances" with OM3 70m and OM4 100m for the supported protocols collectively. Modes might be:
- Not creating fiber-only modes without standard_code pairing.

I'll add a fourth mode only if evidence - I won't.

rx_overload 3.4 and 5.5 unused - DT 3.4 is damage not overload; 5.5 absolute max.

bit_rate 25.78125, 27.95, 28.05 in pool as per-lane - assigned to respective modes via aggregate rates.
